Would you like to play a key role in ensuring a smooth and professional experience for our clients while working at the intersection of energy, data, systems and operations?

About the role

As Client Success Manager, you will become part of the Client Success team in our Energy Asset Integration & Operations department.

The team is responsible for the operational client journey after a contract has been signed. This includes onboarding and offboarding assets, managing master data, coordinating operational processes, and ensuring that the necessary systems, registrations, and stakeholders are aligned.

You will work with renewable and flexible energy assets such as wind turbines, solar parks, batteries, and electric boilers. The role requires you to navigate confidently between clients, commercial colleagues, operational teams and technical systems—and to take responsibility for getting processes safely across the line.

The position is full-time, fixed-term maternity cover expected to run from January through December 2027.

Your primary responsibilities

Onboarding and data management

• Coordinate the onboarding and offboarding of clients and energy assets.

• Collect, import and quality-assure metering data and asset master data. Ensure that internal systems are configured correctly and that the required registrations are completed.

• Coordinate supplier switching and related market processes.

• Follow up with internal and external stakeholders to ensure that onboarding activities are completed on time.

Daily operations and client coordination

• Handle operational requests and questions from clients and colleagues.

• Coordinate outages, redispatch activities, and changes affecting the operation of client assets.

• Identify missing information, clarify uncertainties, and make sure issues are followed through to completion.

• Maintain accurate documentation and ensure that relevant information is available to the teams that depend on it.

• Contribute to a reliable and professional day-to-day experience for our clients.

Cross-functional responsibility and improvements

• Collaborate closely with colleagues in Sales, Trading, Settlement, IT, and other operational teams.

• Coordinate dependencies across teams and ensure clear ownership of outstanding tasks.

• Identify opportunities to simplify, standardise, and automate manual processes.

• Contribute to the further development of our master-data platform and operational tools.

• Explore how automation and AI can improve quality, efficiency, and scalability in the team’s work.

We need a colleague who enjoys working with structure, data and systems, and who takes responsibility for getting processes safely across the line. If you like working in detail, keeping track of many dependencies and at the same time being curious about smarter solutions, you will fit in perfectly here with us.

Anders Borup

Head of Energy Asset Integration & Operations

Who you are

You are structured, thorough, and comfortable working with detailed and data-intensive processes. You take ownership and follow tasks through, even when they involve several systems, teams, and external stakeholders.

At the same time, you are pragmatic and service minded. You communicate clearly, ask questions when something is unclear, and enjoy helping both clients and colleagues find workable solutions.

You do not need to be an energy-market expert from day one. However, you should be curious about the energy sector and motivated to learn how commercial agreements, market processes, data, and physical assets are connected.

We imagine that you

• Have experience in an operational, administrative, analytical, or client-facing role.

• Work systematically and maintain an overview when handling several parallel processes.

• Are comfortable working with data, digital tools and business systems.

• Take independent responsibility for tasks and deadlines.

• Communicate professionally with both clients and internal stakeholders.

• Enjoy collaborating across teams and professional disciplines.

• Are curious about process improvements, automation and the practical use of AI.

• Are fluent in English, both written and spoken. Danish or another European language is an advantage.

Ideally have experience from the energy sector, although this is not a requirement.

Your educational background may be commercial, technical or administrative. Your approach to the work and your ability to create structure and follow through are more important than a specific degree.

We offer

You will join an ambitious energy-trading company operating in a rapidly developing market. You will become part of a collaborative environment with short decision paths, significant responsibility and close interaction between commercial, operational and technical specialists.

The role offers a broad insight into energy trading and the operational management of renewable and flexible assets. Although the position is temporary, you will be given genuine responsibility and the opportunity to make a visible contribution to the team and our clients from the beginning.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Integration of High-Temperature Heat Pumps in Industrial Processes - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Do you want your research to help industry decide how to electrify its heat supply? At DTU Construct you will combine thermodynamics, optimisation and machine learning to build tools that make the business case for industrial high-temperature heat pumps clear, fast and reliable.

We invite applications for a fully funded PhD position in the Thermal Energy Section of the Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark. The position is part of HeatMinds, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by Horizon Europe. HeatMinds brings together 6 universities and research institutes and 12 industrial and research partners across Europe to develop industrial high-temperature heat pumps that upgrade low-grade waste heat to up to about 250 °C.

Your project will address decision making support for heat pump end-users from a first viability check to integration with the process, to flexible operation. You will demonstrate the findings in industrial use cases together with our partners.

Supervision: Prof. Ahmad Arabkoohsar and Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall goal will be, through adequate methodological advancements, to cuts the time and effort needed to assess where and how high-temperature heat pumps should be integrated into industrial sites, and what is their economic value. Your main task will be:

• Develop models to rapidly estimate performance and break-even point for specific sites
• Extent methods for heat pump integration that co-optimize heat recovery, electrification and flexibility provided by heat pumps
• Refine and validate methods during industrial secondments 
• Publish in international journals, present at conferences and take part in HeatMinds network training, summer schools and outreach.
 
You have:

• A solid background in engineering thermodynamics, heat transfer and energy technologies, e.g. conversion or storage systems 
• Familiarity with modelling and numerical simulations, for example for MSc thesis or student projects 
• Programming skills, preferably in Python, Matlab, Modelica or similar 
• Excellent written and spoken English, and the motivation to work in an international, goal-oriented environment.
 
MSCA eligibility: at the time of recruitment, you must not already hold a doctoral degree. You must also not have resided or carried out your main activities (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your recruitment date.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The PhD salary will be based on the Marie S. Curie compensation scheme conditions and according to the grant agreement. Based on seniority the candidate will receive a minimum of DKK 30.264,08 (base salary) and DKK 1580,90 (PhD supplement). In addition, DTU will also pay pension consisting of 18,07%. Finally, it is possible to apply for family allowance. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. Starting date is anticipated as 1 April 2027 or according to mutual agreement. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor Ahmad Arabkoohsar ahmar@dtu.dk and Professor Adriano Sciacovelli adrsc@dtu.dk.

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 24 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A copy of thesis (if available) or other publications (if available)
• A short critical literature review (max. 3 pages) on integration of high-temperature heat in industrial processes: select up to 5 relevant publications and explain your choice, compare their methods & findings, identify possible open research questions, explaining how your background would help you address them. Include at least one figure or table of your own making. 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

Who We Are

For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world's leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 3,500+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds in general.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated in our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

While striving to deliver client value, we believe it is vital to consider our people and our planet in every business decision we make. Acting responsibly is not optional. It is essential.

Why This Role is Important to Us

We are looking for Software Engineers at middle level to join our engineering team that builds fintech solutions for managing OTC (Over-The-Counter) financial instruments within our asset management platform, SimCorp Dimension and SimCorp One. Our work delivers value in two major areas. First, we implement new features that drive the business forward and shape the future of our platform. Second, we focus on extending and maintaining our established solutions to ensure our clients’ operations remain uninterrupted and always available.

What You Will Be Responsible For

• 
Designing, building, and extending existing solutions and APIs for our OTC asset management product, delivering value to customers incrementally.

• 
Working primarily in C#. Our codebase also includes OCaml and APL therefore prior experience with these languages is a strong plus.

• 
Understanding, refactoring and modernizing our legacy codebase without disrupting the business it supports.

• 
Focusing on the systems as a whole and being able address fundamental changes that improves the quality, performance and user experience.

• 
Collaborating closely with your product owner to refine requirements, clarify business needs, and shape how features get built.

• 
Working as part of a team of skilled engineers — pairing, reviewing code, and sharing ownership of the solution with fellow engineers.

• 
Following good engineering practice: clean code, automated testing, and CI/CD.

• 
Building, extending and consuming REST APIs.

• 
Communicating clearly with both technical and business stakeholders.

• 
Continuously learning — and helping the team and product grow with you.

Required Skills & Experience

• Interest in creating innovative features for a complex platform, working on areas such as API scalability, automation, performance, and operational resilience - having space to explore, design and influence the final solution.

• Good C# skills. This is the core language for the role; your level of seniority will determine how much ownership and architectural input you're expected to bring.

• Experience with, or genuine interest in, functional programming. Familiarity with OCaml, APL, F#, Standard ML, Scala or Haskell is a real advantage but not required — a willingness to learn is what matters most.

• Experience (or strong interest) in refactoring existing code and working with legacy systems.

• Good collaboration and communication skills, with fluency in English (written and spoken).

• A relevant degree (Computer Science or STEM) with demonstrated hands-on experience in software engineering.

Furthermore, We Value That You Are:

• motivated to work within the financial domain,

• comfortable working closely with a cross-functional team,

• willing to learn and pick up new languages and paradigms as needed,

• able to identify tech debt and help drive incremental improvement,

• a collaborative person willing to share knowledge and learn from your team members.

Our Team and Ways of Working

We deliver solution for large scale financial institutions with billions of dollars in managed assets. Therefore, our work impacts everyday of our customers operations. You will work in a small team of highly skilled engineers on whole SDLC process – from understanding customers' needs, through solutioning and design to coding, testing and maintaining our software. Our hybrid model of working includes two days (minimum) in our Copenhagen office and up to three days working remotely. Codebase includes a mix of C#, OCaml and APL which gives broad opportunities to upskill and drive your career with us. We invest a lot in your understanding of both the technical details of the solution and financial knowledge that will allow you to contribute to building the future of asset management.

Our Benefits

Competitive salary, bonus scheme, and pension are essential for any work agreement. However, at SimCorp, we believe we can offer more. Therefore, in addition to the traditional benefit scheme, we provide an excellent work-life balance: flexible work hours, a hybrid workplace model. On top of that, we have IP innovation sprints, where you have dedicated time per quarter to spend on mastering your skills as well as contributing to the company development. There is never just one route — we practice an individual approach to professional development to support the direction you want to take.

Next Steps

Please click below to apply. Applications are continuously assessed, so please send your CV in English as soon as possible. If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp but are not sure this role is the right fit, submit your CV anyway. SimCorp is on an exciting growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to help you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks. We are eager to continually improve our talent acquisition process and make everyone's experience positive and valuable. Therefore, during the process, we will ask you to provide your feedback, which is highly appreciated.

Every year, European governments spend billions on mobility: subsidies, contracts, licences, public transport. Most of that money is spent with no clear idea of what it buys for society.

We're building the tech layer that changes that.

What we do

Impact Market builds MIMA, the Mobility Impact Market. On our platform, cities and transport authorities incentivise mobility operators (bike share, e-scooters, car-pooling, car sharing, bike leasing) for trips according to their benefit to society: a car trip replaced, emissions avoided, space and congestion saved, health improved, a neighbourhood connected. By estimating the socio-economic impact of each trip, we design smart incentives that get the most social value out of public funds.

The idea is much bigger than mobility: governments paying for the outcomes they want, with the evidence to back it up. Mobility is our first market, and we intend to move into other areas of public spending.

Where we are

• 
Funded with 12+ months runway

• 
Several paying public-sector clients

• 
A production platform (prod + staging), with live trip and rider-survey data from operators flowing in since August 2026

• 
A team of 3. You'd be number 4.

The role

You'll be our first technical hire and will lead product and engineering. For now that means hands fully dirty: you write the code. No agencies, no outsourcing.

• 
Own the platform. Rust, Postgres, cloud, our RiderSurvey API, and the data pipelines from operators. You'll inherit a working MVP and decide what to keep, what to rebuild and what to build next.

• 
Make the big calls, including the language. We chose Rust deliberately: we think a strict compiler and type system are the right guardrails for building fast with AI. If you have a better argument for something else, convince us.

• 
Be AI-native. We expect you to use AI seriously in coding and every other technical task. That's how a team of four does the work of fifteen.

• 
Build agents that run the company with us, for account management, client reporting and forecasting.

• 
Grow into the science. Together with a future R&D lead, you'll work on the statistical significance of measured impacts and on forecasting how markets respond to incentives.

• 
Shape the product with the founders and our clients. You'll be in the room with transport authorities, not behind a ticket queue.

You

• 
Have minimum 4 years of relevant experience shipping production software, ideally backend or data-heavy systems

• 
Senior and still love writing code every day? Even better.

• 
Know Rust, or are genuinely motivated to go deep in it (not just "willing"). (We are not dogmatic about Rust, but we have a working platform built with care, so changing direction would take strong conviction.)

• 
Already build with AI tools daily and have opinions about how to do it well

• 
Are comfortable with data: SQL, pipelines, and an appetite for statistics and forecasting

• 
Take ownership when things are ambiguous, and like it when nobody tells you how

• 
Care about the mission. You don't need to have read our founder's book, The Next Democracy, but its core ideas about how citizens and governments could work together - is fundamental to what we do. If they don’t excite you, this probably isn't the right fit.

Bonus points for experience in mobility or transport, govtech, causal inference or experimentation, or privacy-by-design and GDPR.

What we offer

A real say in everything. Stack, product, architecture, culture and who we hire next.

• 
Title decided together. We're advertising this as CTO / Founding Engineer and will settle the title with you based on your experience and ambitions.

Competitive startup salary plus a meaningful warrant package, designed to make total compensation comparable with bigger-company offers

5 weeks of holiday and flexible hours

Work that matters. Help redirect public money towards what actually improves people's lives.
